documents.body: My elbows are flaring again with the cold. I'm out of the triamcinolone. Can I get more? Using drugstore lotion in the meantime.

documents.title: RE: Eczema cream
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Refilled, 80 g tube. Twice a day on the patches for up to two weeks, then stop and keep moisturizing. If it keeps coming back in the same spots, come in.

documents.title: Office Visit - eczema
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Eczema has been bad all winter. Itchy patches keep coming back in the same places, both elbow creases mostly. Worse in the cold months and after long hot showers, which he admits he takes. Triamcinolone helps while he's on it, plus drugstore creams and lotions, but it comes right back once he stops. No oozing, no fevers. Breathing fine, albuterol only a couple times in March.

O: Vitals as charted. Afebrile.
Skin: erythematous, scratched patches in both antecubital fossae. No pustules, crusting or vesicles. Rest of skin unremarkable.
Lungs clear.

A/P: Atopic dermatitis, flaring repeatedly this winter despite intermittent mid-potency steroid.
- Dermatology referral for a second opinion on maintenance.
- Continue triamcinolone bid to active areas, then stop.
- He has not had bloodwork in a while and asked for a check before the derm visit: CBC and CMP today.
- Shorter, cooler showers; plain thick moisturizer after.

documents.title: Blood count and chemistry
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Blood count, kidney and liver tests and electrolytes are all normal. I'll forward these to dermatology with the referral.

documents.title: Dermatology consultation
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE DERMATOLOGY GROUP - CONSULTATION LETTER
Date of visit: 04/28/2025
Re: Wyatt Galvin, DOB 12/22/2000
Referred by the primary care physician for recurring eczema.

Thank you for sending this 24-year-old graduate student. He describes a long-standing pruritic eruption that is clearly worse through the winter and after hot showers. Over-the-counter creams give him some relief, and he uses triamcinolone 0.1% for flares, but the rash keeps returning to the same sites. He has not traveled recently, started anything new, or been around anyone ill.

History: seasonal allergic rhinitis, mild persistent asthma, atopic dermatitis since infancy. No surgeries.
Medications: albuterol HFA as needed; cetirizine 10 mg daily; triamcinolone 0.1% cream twice daily as needed.
Allergies: tree, grass and ragweed pollen; dust mites.
Family history: mother with seasonal allergies and eczema; father with asthma; sister with atopic dermatitis.

Examination: Several erythematous patches with overlying excoriation in the flexural folds of both elbows. No pustules, vesicles or drainage. The rest of the skin examination is normal, as is the general examination. Clinical photographs were taken for our record.

Data: CBC and metabolic panel from your office earlier this month, unremarkable.

Impression: Atopic dermatitis, flexural, in flare.

Recommendations:
1. Continue triamcinolone 0.1% cream twice daily to active patches during flares.
2. Fragrance-free emollient liberally after short, lukewarm showers.
Happy to see him again if flares do not settle.

Dermatology

Physical, plus one new issue.

NEW: Since around April, solid food sometimes hangs up behind the breastbone. Meat and bread mostly. Happens maybe once or twice a week, he drinks water and it goes down. Thought it was heartburn, tried Tums-type antacids and then OTC omeprazole 20 mg daily for a few weeks this summer. No change, so he stopped it. Liquids fine. Has not lost weight. No vomiting. Bowels normal. No pain with swallowing.

Chronic: Asthma quiet over the summer, albuterol rarely. Cetirizine daily. Eczema settled after the dermatology visit, moisturizing more.
PHQ-9 3.
Meds: albuterol prn, cetirizine 10 daily, triamcinolone cream prn. Not taking omeprazole.
Never smoker, no alcohol.

EXAM: vitals as charted, weight unchanged from last year. Oropharynx clear. Neck supple, no masses. Lungs clear. Heart regular, no murmur. Abdomen soft and nontender, no masses. Skin: elbows clear today.

A/P
1. Intermittent dysphagia to solids, about five months, not helped by acid suppression. Young atopic man - want an endoscopy. GI referral placed. Advised small bites, chew well, liquids with meals.
2. Asthma, rhinitis, eczema - stable, no changes.
3. Flu/covid at a nurse visit next month.

reports.text:
Specimens: (A) proximal esophagus, biopsies; (B) distal esophagus, biopsies; (C) stomach, biopsies; (D) duodenum, biopsies.
A, B: Squamous mucosa with intraepithelial eosinophils exceeding 15 per high-power field. No viral cytopathic change. PAS stain negative for fungal organisms.
C: Gastric mucosa without significant abnormality.
D: Duodenal mucosa with normal villous architecture.
reports.conclusion: Esophagus, proximal and distal: eosinophil-predominant esophagitis, more than 15 eosinophils per high-power field, consistent with eosinophilic esophagitis in the appropriate clinical setting. Stomach and duodenum: no abnormality.

documents.title: Gastroenterology consultation and endoscopy
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY GROUP
Consultation and procedure, 10/27/2025
Patient: Wyatt Galvin, 24 y/o M
Reason: solid-food dysphagia, referred by PCP

HPI: Six months of on-and-off trouble getting solids down, with a feeling that food lodges in the chest. He self-treated with antacids and then a PPI on the assumption it was heartburn; neither changed anything. Denies weight loss, vomiting or change in bowel habit.
Background: allergic rhinitis, mild persistent asthma, atopic dermatitis seen by dermatology this spring. No surgeries.
Meds: albuterol as needed; cetirizine 10 mg daily; triamcinolone 0.1% cream as needed.
Allergies: pollens (tree, grass, ragweed), dust mites.
Family: mother with atopic dermatitis.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol, graduate student.
Exam: unremarkable.

PROCEDURE: EGD with biopsies, same day. Moderate sedation. Scope passed to the second part of the duodenum. Esophageal mucosa without stated abnormality on inspection; stomach and duodenum normal. Biopsies from proximal and distal esophagus, stomach and duodenum.

PATHOLOGY (resulted 10/30): esophageal squamous epithelium with more than 15 eosinophils per HPF, no viral inclusions or fungal organisms; gastric and duodenal biopsies normal.

IMPRESSION: Eosinophilic esophagitis.
We will see him back in clinic.

Gastroenterology

documents.title: Question about my scope results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: GI says I have eosinophilic esophagitis. Is that connected to my allergies and eczema? Is it something serious?

documents.title: RE: Question about my scope results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good question. Yes, it belongs to the same allergic family as your asthma, hay fever and eczema - allergy-type white cells collect in the lining of the esophagus and make it stiff and irritable, which is why food hangs up. It is not cancer and it is very manageable. GI will go over options with you at the follow-up. Until then keep the small bites and plenty of liquid with meals.

REGIONAL HOSPITAL ED - PHYSICIAN RECORD (received by fax)
Arrival 04/22/2026 18:40   Disposition: home 23:05

CC: vomiting after eating, food getting stuck

HPI: 25 yo M, allergic rhinitis, mild persistent asthma, atopic dermatitis, eosinophilic esophagitis diagnosed by GI in the fall. Intermittent trouble swallowing solids for about a year, getting worse over the last six months, with food that feels stuck in the chest. Occasional epigastric discomfort. Two times in the past month he has vomited after a meal; came in tonight after the second. Not currently impacted, tolerating sips of water here.

PMH as above. No surgeries.
Meds: albuterol prn, cetirizine 10 mg daily, triamcinolone 0.1% cream prn.
Allergies: seasonal pollens, dust mites.
FHx: non-contributory.
SHx: no tobacco, alcohol or drugs.

Exam: well appearing, no distress. Oropharynx clear, handling secretions. Neck supple, no crepitus. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, nontender. No pallor. Weight stable by his account.

Labs: CBC within normal range, no anemia.

MDM: Progressive dysphagia with post-prandial vomiting in a patient with known EoE. No impaction, no signs of perforation, stable. Needs endoscopic reassessment.

Dispo: discharged. Soft diet, cut food small, sit upright. Call GI tomorrow for an urgent appointment - message left for the on-call GI group. Return for food stuck and unable to swallow saliva, chest pain, or blood in vomit.

Emergency Medicine

Eosinophilic esophagitis, worsening, with recent post-meal vomiting. Repeat EGD 5/6 with GI; treatment to follow from them. Soft diet in the meantime. Return or ED if food impacts.
Asthma, rhinitis, eczema stable.
Follow up in about two months.

documents.title: Gastroenterology endoscopy and follow-up letter
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY GROUP
Procedure date 05/06/2026
Patient: Wyatt Galvin
Indication: eosinophilic esophagitis with progressive solid dysphagia and two episodes of post-meal vomiting, ED visit 04/22.
Allergies: pollens (tree, grass, ragweed), dust mites.

EGD: Moderate sedation. Multiple concentric rings and linear furrows along the length of the esophagus. Scope passed without resistance. Stomach and duodenum normal. Biopsies from proximal and distal esophagus.

Pathology 05/08: more than 20 eosinophils per HPF in esophageal mucosa.

Assessment: Eosinophilic esophagitis, active, with rings and furrows on endoscopy.

Plan:
- Started budesonide oral suspension 2 mg (10 mL) swallowed twice daily. Nothing by mouth for 30 minutes after each dose.
- Repeat endoscopy with biopsies after the course to assess response.
- Clinic visit in about 10 weeks.

Gastroenterology

documents.title: GI letter received
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Got the GI letter and biopsy results. I've added the budesonide to your medication list here. Swallow it, don't rinse, and hold food and drink for half an hour after. Let me know how swallowing is going over the next few weeks.

documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks. Pharmacy had it ready after the GI office sorted the insurance. Started Monday.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Two-month follow-up.

Esophagus: about eight weeks into budesonide. Food catches much less - maybe once a week, and passes easily. No vomiting at all since May. Taking it twice a day, waits the half hour. No mouth soreness or white patches.
Asthma: spring went ok, albuterol a few times a week in May, now rarely. No night symptoms.
Allergies: cetirizine daily, fine.
Skin: elbows quiet this summer.

Meds reviewed: budesonide oral suspension 2 mg bid; albuterol HFA prn; cetirizine 10 mg daily; triamcinolone 0.1% cream prn.

Exam: vitals as charted, weight stable. Mouth and throat without thrush. Lungs clear, no wheeze. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, nontender.

A/P
1. Eosinophilic esophagitis - responding on swallowed budesonide. GI follow-up later this month, repeat scope after the course.
2. Mild persistent asthma - unchanged, albuterol as needed.
3. Allergic rhinitis, atopic dermatitis - stable.
See him in September, after the repeat scope. Flu and covid due this fall.
